answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity revalidate every epoch through a notary. The notary captures a zephyr—a short head turn—hashes the biometric, and stores it as a vertex in a deduplication graph; any template matching an existing vertex is rejected, so the registry is not an ocean of interchangeable entries. The registry charges a revalidation fee C per epoch and caps identities at K. With per-epoch reward R, n sybils pay nC and earn at most nR, so cloning is unprofitable when C>R. Assumption: notaries' dedup and bond slashing work; colluding notaries are the weakness.
